endorsements.quote: This phased structure allows for iterative refinement and ensures that stakeholder perspectives are embedded throughout the lifecycle of AI deployment.

To steer this process, Phase 1 involves establishing a partnership table that includes senior leaders from the provincial government health care agencies; clinicians from local hospitals, primary care networks and family health teams; community-based organizations and public health agencies; as well as patients and caregivers with lived experience of Type 2 diabetes and the healthcare system.

In subsequent Phase 3 of tool operationalization, our team and partners will co-design a visual analytics dashboard for end users to facilitate the use of the diabetes AI prediction models for population health assessment and the planning of diabetes prevention and management strategies.
Working collaboratively with our partnership table, in Phase 2, we complete a needs assessment to understand the context in which the diabetes AI tools will be implemented.
(2) establish feedback mechanisms to monitor stakeholder trust and acceptability during implementation
(3) invest in governance infrastructure that ensures accountability and responsiveness to ethical and social considerations throughout the AI lifecycle.

unlisted_practices: Embed co-design and evaluation as integral components of AI deployment rather than add-on activities.
Conduct an ethical audit of AI models informed by responsible AI principles to identify algorithmic biases for population subgroups and inform iterative model improvements.
Measure stakeholder-perceived trustworthiness and acceptability of AI tools during evaluation.

screen.reason: This is a commentary presenting recommendations and a framework for participatory approaches and stakeholder co-design to deploy responsible AI for diabetes risk prediction.
